summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, Chün-fang Yü studied at Columbia University (~1965–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001; Sheng Yen Professor Emerita attested 2026).

Clara Sue Kidwell worked in history and archaeology, earning her master's and Ph.D. at the University of Oklahoma (~1963–1970). Her career included positions at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London in ~2011.

Linguist Claude Hagège studied at the École Normale Supérieure, ENLOV, and under André Martinet. He held posts at the CNRS, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1988), the University of Poitiers (1970–1987), and the Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under George Cœdès (~1955–1969). He served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1997).

A scholar in philosophy and other fields, Claude Lévi-Strauss studied under Marcel Mauss (~1930–1935). He held appointments at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1950–1974), EHESS (~1948–1982), and the Collège de France (1959–1982).

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Claude-Auguste Court studied at the École polytechnique and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1813–1814). Between ~1827 and 1843, he served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army and Court of Ranjit Singh.
Claudia Benthien is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. She studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~2005).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he was appointed Vice-Provost of Fort William College.

Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, completing his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1969–1983). He taught at Hamburg (~1974–1987) and led the Indology department at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel worked in Indology and Tibetology, completing his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Marburg, and studying at Deccan College. He held professorial posts at Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar based at the University of Canterbury, where she held posts in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.
Clinton B. Seely was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he became Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).

Clyde Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin–Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard (~1934–1936). He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Indologist and linguist Colette Caillat studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at the CNRS (~1956–1966), University of Lyon (1960–1966), Sorbonne (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1972–1990).

Colette Sciberras works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.
Colin Mackenzie studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1810 to 1815.
Colin Turnbull was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Westminster School (~1937–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).
